modelingNotes: Urban District Market (Lintmen's), 2315 N Davidson St, NoDa / Villa Heights, Charlotte — procedural, CC0-1.0. bun generators/clt-urban-district-market.ts

The former Lawrence Knitting Mills (1950s), later a cork works, an auto shop and a concrete plant, reopened in 2022-23 as Lintmen's, with the Urban District Market food hall in its north-western half and shops and a gym in the rest. One tall storey of red brick under two side-by-side shallow barrel vaults of pale membrane, running the length of the building. What makes it itself, each drawn as plain geometry: - the twin barrel roofs, their arches showing on the end walls; - red brick walls with a black band along the top; - the greenway (north-west) end: the solid "FOOD HALL" corner bay, the porch under a sloping metal canopy with tall black-framed openings, and the entrance at the top of its stairs under the tall weathering-steel frame carrying the "Urban District Market" letters (lettering not modelled; the frame and its rails are), beside a lower brick wing; - on the North Davidson Street (south-east) end, the vaults sloping down behind a plain parapet.

Map frame: x across the building (north-east +, 46.6°), y along it (bearing 316.6, the outline's long axis: + toward the greenway), z up, metres. Origin = centroid of OSM way/323201452, lng -80.8144199, lat 35.2407037.

Evidence: - OSM way/323201452 (building, height 9, 2315 N Davidson St): 45.5 × 58-71 m. The food court, way/1105368103 (amenity=food_court, not a building), is its north-western half; the shops' nodes sit in the rest. - Lidar, USGS 3DEP USGS_LPC_NC_Phase4_Mecklenburg_2016 (flown 2016-17, before the 2022 conversion), 0.5 m grid sampled in this frame: two barrel vaults split at the outline's jog (x = -1.2): the south-west one 22.4 m wide, eaves 6.0 m and crown 8.3 m above y = 0 at x = -12; the north-east one 23.2 m wide, crown 7.7 m at x = 10. They end at y = 25.4 (south-west) and 30.3 (north-east) at the greenway end; a 5.1 m flat strip (the canopy and corner bay) runs to the outline at y = 27.4; the entrance wing (x 12-22, y 30-40) is flat at 4.7 m. At the street end the vaults slope down over their last 3.5 m to a 6.4 m parapet. A narrow 8 m return at the jog just outside the street front (a pole or a sign, gone or unidentified) is left out. Ground: ground_min 207.00 m at the north-west; y = 0 is ground_min + 1.1 m, rising 2.2 m to the street end. The lidar footprint matches the OSM outline. - USGS NAIP: the pale roof over the whole outline, two vaults. - Published: Charlotte-Mecklenburg Historic Landmarks Commission news, 10 Sep 2020 ("Lawrence Knitting Mills Gaining New Life as Food Hall"); lintmens.com (Lawrence Knitting Mills, 1950s, later uses; Cluck Design Collaborative); Liles Construction (completed October 2022); Axios Charlotte 2023-04-13 (food hall opened April 2023). - Photos (Wikimedia Commons, City Dweller 2, CC BY-SA 4.0): · "Urban District Market Porch Late March 2024.jpg" — the greenway end from the west: the FOOD HALL bay, porch and canopy, both vaults' arches, the steel sign frame beyond. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Urban_District_Market_Porch_Late_March_2024.jpg · "Urban District Market Sign Late March 2024.jpg" — the entrance in the north-east vault's end wall head-on: the frame, door, windows, black band, brick. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Urban_District_Market_Sign_Late_March_2024.jpg · "Little Sugar Creek Greenway Urban District Section at 26th St Early March 2025.jpg" — the same end from the greenway: flat-topped end walls with the pale vault ends rising behind them, the frame. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Little_Sugar_Creek_Greenway_Urban_District_Section_at_26th_St_Early_March_2025.jpg

Numbers: plan from OSM; every roof and wall height from lidar. Estimated from the head-on entrance photo, scaled by its 1.8 m double door (111 px/m): the 1.6 m landing, the door, windows and lintels, the frame (3.56 m wide; top 9.8 m, the photo looking up, so a lower bound; 2016 lidar predates it) and its rails; the porch's 1.1 m floor, the canopy's slope and the 0.45 m black band from the porch photo. The end walls are flat-topped at the eaves with the vault ends showing above them, as both greenway photos show. The valley gutter is drawn 1.8 m wide, broader than the real one, so the two vaults read apart at phone size.

Doubts: no licensed photo shows the North Davidson Street end, the 26th Street (south-west) side or the north-east side. Those walls are drawn plain brick with the black band, no openings; the street end's sloping vault ends are the 2016 lidar's and may have changed in 2022. Mapillary was not available. The FOOD HALL and sign letters are left out.

Original procedural model from https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks (catalog id "clt-urban-district-market", model "clt-urban-district-market"), generated by https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks/blob/a1974bbf738c6994edbe99a7a61818b9d69da9e0/generators/clt-urban-district-market.ts. That repository is the editable source; source.blend.gz is the exported mesh imported into Blender for convenience.

Exported for Open Landmarks v1: placement bearing and scale baked in; moving parts frozen in their rest pose; footings and basements below the lowest ground (y = 0) cut away; material colours carried over exactly, as library finishes where they are not standard swatches.
